identification.summary: UNC3569 is Mandiant's (Google Threat Intelligence) uncategorized-cluster designation for a China-nexus espionage actor observed exploiting vulnerabilities in Aspera Faspex, Microsoft Exchange and Oracle Web Applications Desktop Integrator, among others, to gain initial access [S2]. Google researchers describe it as one of the more prolific China-nexus actors and say its GRAYRABBIT backdoor is among its favored tools [S3]. In September 2026 Gen Threat Labs reported UNC3569 exploiting a Tencent Sogou Input Method flaw to deploy GRAYRABBIT [S5][S6].
identification.firstObserved: Google/Virus Bulletin 2024 listing: targeting observed since 2021 [S3]. Google has tracked UNC3569 since 2021 per press coverage [S5].
identification.notes: UNC3569 is a Mandiant cluster, not a Microsoft-named actor; no Microsoft name is stated in the sources gathered. Mandiant suspects with moderate confidence that UNC5266 (Ivanti exploitation cluster) overlaps in part with UNC3569; keep the clusters separate [S2]. The Virus Bulletin paper reportedly discusses possible links to UNC251 and UNC3246 [S1].

attribution.sponsor: China-nexus (Mandiant wording) [S2]. The Virus Bulletin 2024 abstract, as listed by Thinkst Citation, describes the actor as operating in the MSS ecosystem and discusses front or shell companies [S3]. Press coverage of Google's assessment describes it as a hacker-for-hire actor [S5]. No government attribution found.
attribution.confidence: Mandiant: 'China-nexus espionage actor' [S2]. The 'suspected moderate confidence' statement in the sources applies only to the partial UNC5266 overlap [S2].
attribution.basis: Google/Mandiant analysis presented at Virus Bulletin 2024 (full paper not opened) [S1][S3]; Mandiant April 2024 Ivanti blog [S2]; Gen Threat Labs observation of the Sogou exploit in a live intrusion via secondary coverage [S5][S6].

objectives: Espionage, consistent with the Mandiant characterization as a China-nexus espionage actor [S2]. Targeting of government, education, high-tech and financial organizations since 2021 [S3].

regions: Mostly East and Southeast Asia (per press coverage of Google's description) [S5]
targeting.notes: Sectors from the Virus Bulletin 2024 abstract [S3]. Regions from The Hacker News summary [S5]. The Mandiant Ivanti blog gives no UNC3569 victim list [S2]. Specific victims of the 2026 Sogou activity are not described in the coverage reviewed [S5][S6].

capabilities.summary: Initial access through exploitation of internet-facing enterprise software including Aspera Faspex, Microsoft Exchange and Oracle Web Applications Desktop Integrator [S2]. The Virus Bulletin abstract says the actor has used vulnerability scanners to exploit CVE-2021-34523, CVE-2021-34473, CVE-2021-31207 (Exchange ProxyShell-era) and CVE-2022-21587 (Oracle Web ADI) [S3]. GRAYRABBIT is a lightweight backdoor supporting file operations, system information collection, modular plugins and a remote command shell, and is among the actor's favored tools [S3]. In 2026 the actor exploited CVE-2026-51990, a one-click RCE in Tencent Sogou Input Method for Windows via the sgbiz: URI handler loading an attacker page in an embedded outdated Chromium, chained with CVE-2021-38003 per secondary reporting, to deploy GRAYRABBIT [S5][S6][S7]. Tencent shipped version 16.3.0.3498 on 2026-04-21 after Gen reported the flaw on 2026-04-09 [S6].

campaigns.summary: Google data shows targeting of government, education, high-tech and financial organizations since 2021, using vulnerability scanners and exploits for Exchange and Oracle Web ADI flaws.

campaigns.name: Mandiant publishes UNC3569 / UNC5266 overlap
campaigns.summary: Mandiant's Ivanti post-exploitation blog describes UNC3569 as exploiting Aspera Faspex, Exchange and Oracle Web ADI and assesses with moderate confidence that UNC5266 partially overlaps it.

campaigns.name: Virus Bulletin 2024 presentation
campaigns.summary: Google researchers present 'Down the GRAYRABBIT hole' on UNC3569, its tooling and possible links to other clusters.

campaigns.name: Sogou Input Method flaw reported and patched
campaigns.summary: Gen reported the flaw to Tencent on 9 April; fixed version 16.3.0.3498 shipped 21 April. Gen found the flaw while investigating a live UNC3569 intrusion.

campaigns.name: Gen Threat Labs reports in-the-wild CVE-2026-51990 exploitation
campaigns.summary: Gen reports UNC3569 abusing the Sogou flaw to deploy GRAYRABBIT with a single click; Gen said the embedded Chromium configuration remained unchanged as of 10 September. Coverage dates differ by a few days.

diamond.adversary: China-nexus espionage cluster tracked by Mandiant/Google; described in Google research as part of the MSS-linked contractor ecosystem [S2][S3].
diamond.capability: Public-exploit initial access, vulnerability scanning, GRAYRABBIT backdoor, and 2026 Sogou one-click RCE [S2][S3][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Not detailed in the sources reviewed. The April 2024 Mandiant blog attributes tooling (SLIVER, WARPWIRE, TERRIBLETEA) only to the partially overlapping UNC5266 [S2].
diamond.victim: Government, education, high-tech and financial organizations, mostly East and Southeast Asia [S3][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Espionage in support of PRC-nexus intelligence interests; contractor-style operation [S2][S3][S5].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing file-transfer, mail and ERP-adjacent servers (Aspera Faspex, Exchange, Oracle Web ADI) and a widely installed Windows input-method application with an embedded outdated Chromium [S2][S3][S7].

gaps: Primary Mandiant/Google documents (Virus Bulletin paper, Gen Threat Labs report) could not be opened; WebFetch failed on virusbulletin.com and other hosts, so details rely on search summaries and secondary coverage.

A search summary of the Virus Bulletin paper stated shared connections with i-SOON including an i-SOON-linked IP address; this was not confirmed in the abstract text reviewed and should be verified against the paper before use.
Aspera Faspex CVE not identified in the sources reviewed.
Relationship with UNC5266, UNC251 and UNC3246 is partial or suspected only; do not merge clusters [S1][S2].
Victim identities, dwell times and objectives beyond sector-level espionage are not public in sources reviewed.
CISA KEV status of CVE-2026-51990 was reported inconsistently by secondary sources.
Publication date of the Gen report varies across coverage (10-13 September 2026).
No Microsoft actor name or MITRE group ID found.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing Exchange, file-transfer (Aspera Faspex) and Oracle web application servers, plus endpoints running Sogou Input Method, are candidate key terrain in organizations with East or Southeast Asia exposure [S2][S3][S5]. STEP 2: The actor targets government, education, high-tech and finance, and has reused 2021-2022 vulnerabilities for years, so unpatched legacy systems stay exposed [S3]. STEP 3: Template is vulnerability scanning, exploit of an internet-facing server, GRAYRABBIT deployment, then remote shell, file collection and plugins [S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued opportunistic exploitation of unpatched enterprise servers for espionage in Asia-Pacific government and technology targets. MDCOA is use of the Sogou-style one-click client-side route against coalition or partner-nation personnel using Chinese-language software. Candidate indicators: Sogou sgbiz: URI invocations spawning processes, unexpected Sogou-parent child processes, ProxyShell-pattern Exchange requests, web shells on Exchange/Oracle hosts [S3][S5][S7].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track CVE-2026-51990 patch state (16.3.0.3498) and the unchanged Chromium risk on partner and contractor endpoints in the Indo-Pacific [S6]. (2) Authorities: patching or removing software on partner or contractor networks needs owner-network authority, so route requests through system owners and DC3/DIB channels. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize patching legacy Exchange and Oracle Web ADI instances on mission-supporting networks [S3]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with Mandiant/Google and coalition partners, noting UNC5266 overlap is only partial [S2].
